subject: weird behavior of ggplot with unique continuous parameter value

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: weird behavior of ggplot with unique continuous parameter value
parts:
Dear all,

Consider the following,

library(ggplot2)

d1 <- data.frame(x=1:10, y=rnorm(10), f=1)
d2 <- data.frame(x=1:10, y=rnorm(10), f="1")
d3 <- data.frame(x=1:10, y=rnorm(10), f=rep(1:2, each=5))

p <- ggplot(d1) +
geom_point(aes(x,y))

p1 <- p + aes(colour=f)
p2 <- p1 %+% d2
p3 <- p1 %+% d3
p4 <- p + aes(shape=f)
p5 <- p1 + aes(shape=f)

# library(gridExtra)
# arrange(p, p1, p2, p3, p4, p5)

I don't understand plots p1, p4 and p5.

First, the points in p1 and p5 are invisible, this seems to be the
case when an aesthetic is mapped onto a continuous variable with a
single unique value.

Second, I'm surprised that p4 would not show a legend whilst the others do.

Are these known issues (perhaps fixed in the latest version)?

Regards,

baptiste

messages.author: 20823a3be7eac92d
messages.subject: RE: weird behavior of ggplot with unique continuous parameter value
parts:
Hi,

I've just seen the bug report. Clearly, f being a number or factor matters, but solely for the default mapping of the aesthetic. So, you'd expect that if you use the scale_gradient functions the dots should be back in the plot, because a numeric value mapped to the aesthetic should be expected, as in:

p1 <- p + aes(colour=f) + scale_colour_gradientn(colour = rainbow(7))
p1 <- p + aes(colour=f) + scale_colour_gradient(limits=c(0,1))

I don't know if this is relevant to the nature of the bug. I would expect this to work too, but it doesn't:
p1 <- p + aes(colour=f) + scale_colour_gradient(limits=c(1,1))

Leo
